patients.label: 77-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis and CAD after TAVR, with worsening heart failure and leaflet thrombosis

identity_evidence.quote: A 77-year-old man with severe AS and coronary artery disease (CAD)

attribution_limitations: The interval from NOAC treatment to the follow-up MDCT showing resolution is printed as 4 months in the case text and as three months in the abstract; the Figure 2 caption also gives 3 months.

Morbid obesity and the difficulty of TEE evaluation are stated in a present-tense discussion sentence ("it is difficult to evaluate HALT or RLM by TEE") that follows the sentence about this patient's TEE; the sentence does not literally name the patient, so both are review_only.

The discussion describes the echocardiographic gradient series qualitatively (normal immediately post-TAVR, abnormal increase, returning to normal) while the case text gives numeric gradients at a day after TAVR, in the increased state and on follow-up; the source does not say these are the same time points.

The antiplatelet medication is called single antiplatelet medication when rivaroxaban was added, the discussion says dual antiplatelet therapy was followed by single antiplatelet use, and clopidogrel is named only in the bleeding sentence; the source does not state these are the same drug or course.
The 47 mmHg gradient sentence gives no measurement method or timing relative to TAVR, and no dose is given for rivaroxaban.
The discussion states that guidelines recommend warfarin for a bioprosthetic valve with new-onset atrial fibrillation and that the authors chose NOAC instead; no warfarin was reported as given.
The hemoglobin value is printed as 7.2 mg/dl; the unit is kept as printed and may be a one-character print artefact.

evidence.quote: (A) Echocardiogram showing a baseline trans-aortic valve mean pressure gradient of 15 mmHg 1 day after trans-aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

(B) One year later, the patient developed a worsening heart failure, new onset of atrial fibrillation, and an increase of echocardiography-derived mean trans-aortic valve pressure gradient of 48 mmHg.
(C) After 3-month treatment with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anti-coagulant, echocardiogram showing a mean trans-aortic valve pressure gradient of 17 mmHg.
(A) Systolic phase, two-dimensional (2D), short-axis view showing a hypo-attenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) suggestive of thrombus involving the base of leaflets (red arrows).
(B) Systolic phase, 2D, short-axis view showing the resolution of HALT
(C) Diastolic, 2-D, short-axis view showing HALT suggestive of thrombus involving the base of leaflets (red arrows).
(D) Diastolic phase, 2D, short-axis view showing resolution of HALT
(E) Systolic phase, 2D, long-axis view showing HALT suggestive of thrombus involving the base of leaflets (red arrows) and reduced systolic leaflet motion.
(F) Systolic phase, 2D, long-axis view showing resolution of HALT and resumed normal systolic leaflet motion
(G) Diastolic phase, 2D, long-axis view showing HALT suggestive of thrombus involving the base of leaflets (red arrows).
(H) Diastolic phase, 2D, long-axis view showing the resolution of HALT

limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the two JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual target.
Follow-up MDCT interval after NOAC treatment conflicts (4 months in case text, three months in abstract and Figure 2 caption); both sides review_only and the interval is not asserted.
Values printed inside the echocardiographic images are pixel content in the visual target only, not facts.
Hemoglobin unit printed as mg/dl is kept literally; rivaroxaban dose and the identity of the single antiplatelet drug are not stated.
Discussion sentences about cited trials, meta-analyses and guidelines are not patient facts; the supplement Data_Sheet_1.PDF is listed by the source but its contents are reviewed separately.
